ref.description: Pinned doctrine reference: sha256:<hex> digest or absolute path. Digest preferred for provenance.

product.description: Adapter key. Products are invoked only through their contracts.

evidence.description: Operator-local evidence files or directories rendered into the brief's evidence_roots; the downstream review product snapshots them. Empty or absent = no evidence.

protocol.description: Wire protocol binding for a real product runtime. Only A2A v1.0 (JSON-RPC over HTTP) is supported today.

endpoint.description: Agent JSON-RPC endpoint URL. Never a local path; real runtimes are remote products.

card_url.description: Agent Card URL. Defaults to <endpoint origin>/.well-known/agent-card.json.

token_env.description: Name of an environment variable holding the bearer token sent as Authorization. Credentials are never inlined in pipeline specs.

card_sha256.description: Optional pre-pinned Agent Card digest. A fetched card that digests differently halts the stage (fail closed).

in.description: Artifact names produced by earlier stages. Cycles are rejected at validation time.

adapter.description: fake = offline canned receipts. product = shipped HIGHBALL/GALAHAD CLI. Default: product for highball/galahad, fake for doctrine. quinte ignores this and requires runtime.

workdir.description: Product working directory. GALAHAD uses the galahad-futures project root. HIGHBALL does not read workdir evidence: its route request and residual trace are typed, declared upstream artifacts.

engine.description: GALAHAD execution backend selection (run_paper.py --engine). paper = reference book (default). nautilus = NautilusTrader 1.231.0 event-driven backtest engine; requires the optional dependency in the galahad-futures tree, and a missing package is a hard error (no silent fallback).

gate.description: Gate id resolved from the doctrine pack.

on_block.description: Terminal mapping when the product refuses (e.g. HIGHBALL DENIED).

timeout_seconds.description: Per-stage wall-clock budget for a real product invocation; expiry halts the run without cancelling the product.

poll_seconds.description: Interval between one-shot host status polls for a real product invocation.
